observations: Accepted StateFingerprint v2 deliberately rejects float projection values rather than coercing them.
PredictionContract generation 1 deliberately accepts finite float leaves and computes same-type numeric float residuals.
Therefore the new typed StateFingerprint binding path has a strictly narrower projection domain than the legacy PredictionContract projection domain unless generation 2 makes that boundary explicit.
F2-WP-202 generation 2 is forbidden from mutating F2-WP-201, so widening StateFingerprint's domain is not available inside this claim.
risk: A silent typed-to-legacy fallback, coercion, or partial fingerprint can make a prediction appear StateFingerprint-bound when the exact projection was never admissible under the accepted fingerprint ABI.
hypothesis: The typed binding path should explicitly fail closed for projections outside the accepted StateFingerprint domain while the separately named legacy explicit-hash compatibility path remains available; callers must be able to tell which path produced the contract/residual.
counterhypothesis: Generation 2 may define the typed path only for the StateFingerprint-compatible subset and retain all float-bearing predictions exclusively on the legacy path, in which case no defect exists if the distinction is explicit, test-covered, and cannot silently downgrade.
cheapest_discriminator: Regression: create a valid legacy PredictionContract whose projection contains finite float 1.5; prove that requesting typed StateFingerprint binding either rejects with an explicit domain error and no typed contract is produced, or follows an explicitly distinct compatibility route. Also prove no float->int/string coercion and no silent typed->legacy downgrade.
next_exact_action: Active F2-WP-202 mutation authority should include the cross-domain regression in its deterministic suite before component-CI reconciliation.
